questions.prompt: A new order arrives and should be added to a sheet and confirmed by email, the same way every time. What should you build?
options: An agent that decides the best steps for each order
An automation with a trigger and fixed steps
A chatbot that customers can ask about the order
A managed agent that runs every night in the cloud
questions.explanation: Same steps every time, triggered by an event, is an automation. Use the simplest thing that does the job.

questions.prompt: When is an agent the right choice over an automation?
options: When the job must run the same way every single time
When you want the cheapest and fastest possible result
When the steps change each time and judgment is needed
When a customer needs a quick answer at midnight
questions.explanation: Agents decide their own steps, which suits goals that need judgment. For fixed steps, an automation is cheaper and more reliable.

questions.prompt: Your Opal app drafts a reply to a customer's WhatsApp order. What should happen next?
options: You read the draft and send it yourself
Opal sends it straight away to save time
A second AI checks it, then sends it on
It is posted on your Instagram for others
questions.explanation: An agent may draft anything. Nothing leaves without a person approving it.

questions.prompt: Why set a spend limit on your API account before building an agent?
options: The account will not create keys until you set one
A spend limit makes the model answer much faster
It is needed to connect the API to your website
It caps what any mistake or busy week can cost
questions.explanation: Agents and chatbots are billed by use. A limit means a loop gone wrong, or a sudden rush, can never cost more than you chose.

A standard way to plug tools into AI apps
A setting that makes an agent run on a schedule
A type of database for storing chat history
questions.explanation: MCP is a standard plug: a tool that offers an MCP server can be connected to any AI app that supports it.

questions.prompt: Your agent is connected to Gmail. What is the safest way to set it up?
options: Let it send replies to customers without asking
Connect it only after a full day of testing
Let it write drafts, and you send them yourself
Give it access to your bank so it can check payments
questions.explanation: Drafts, not sends. A wrong email to fifty customers costs trust an apology cannot buy back.

questions.prompt: In your AI operating system, what is the routing table for?
options: Telling the agent which files to load for each kind of task
Listing every single website that the agent is allowed to visit
Showing how much each agent has cost you this month
Deciding which model to use for each type of question
questions.explanation: It maps kinds of work to the context files they need, so answers stay focused and each session reads only what it needs.

questions.prompt: You correct your agent: you stopped selling carrot cake. How do you make sure it remembers next week?
options: Repeat the correction at the start of every session
Start a brand new folder for the new cake menu
Ask it to add the change to context/memory.md
Turn off memory so it cannot learn anything wrong
questions.explanation: Corrections are lost when a session ends unless they are written down. The memory file is where the agent writes them, and you check it.

questions.prompt: Your n8n automation runs on your laptop at 7am, but no plan arrived. What is the most likely reason?
options: n8n only allows one scheduled run on the free version
Your laptop or n8n was not running at 7am that day
Scheduled triggers only work in Zapier and Make
The AI step needs a new API key for every run
questions.explanation: On your laptop, schedules run only while the laptop is on and n8n is running. Check Executions, and use the cloud trial for round-the-clock runs.

questions.prompt: A job advert asks for Zapier experience. You have built workflows in n8n. What is the best answer?
options: Say you have never used automation tools at all
Claim years of Zapier experience to get the job
Refuse the job because the tool is not n8n
Explain your n8n work and how it maps to a Zap
questions.explanation: The idea is the same across tools. Name what you really built, and show you can translate it: that tells an employer you understand automation, not one app.
